To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IAP is required for alpha v beta 1 and alpha v beta 5 to bind vitronectin-coated particles and that the IAP immunoglobulin domain suffices for this interaction.
IAP is necessary for efficient Vn bead binding by integrins.
IAP is required for alpha v beta 1-mediated binding of Vn-coated beads to cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of integrin associated protein (IAP) in the regulation of integrin function in phagocytic cells.
the role of IAP in the adhesion of leukocytes and other cells to the extracellular matrix (ECM).
the role of integrin-associated protein (CD47) in the regulation of integrin-mediated cell adhesion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IAP is a ligand for the alpha v beta3 integrin and that IAP is necessary for efficient Vn binding to alpha v beta3.
IAP is required for efficient Vn particle binding through alpha v beta 1 integrin.
IAP is required for efficient binding to Vn beads.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IAP is a ligand for integrins, and it is necessary for some but not all alpha v integrin functions.
IAP is a ligand- binding subunit of integrins, but it is not a subunit of all integrins.
the IAP Ig domain functions as a ligand binding site for the alpha v beta3 integrin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IAP plays a role in the adhesion of cells to Vn, and this adhesion can be mediated by the IAP Ig domain.
IAP is not a general integrin-associated protein but rather is specifically involved in the binding of Vn and related ligands to alpha v beta 1 integrins.
the integrin-associated protein ( IAP ) is necessary for efficient binding of vitronectin beads to cells expressing alpha v-beta 3 integrin.
